title_clean: How to Lose More in the Stock Market
summary: Case study of a friend's leverage death spiral: doubled position pledged for loans, collateral limit reused to sell puts whose premium bought more shares - then a 3-4%/day fall triggered margin calls on both stock and F&O. Teaches portfolio separation, hedging, SWP profit booking, and leverage limits.
lessons: Pledged shares + leveraged F&O is a double kill: falling prices cut portfolio value AND collateral value, triggering margin calls on both.
Option premium received is not profit - it is a liability that may have to be returned many times over.
Book partial profits on the way up (SWP); at +100%, selling 20-50% makes the rest a free position.
A cheap long-dated put financed by a covered call caps portfolio loss (~2% of capital) - insurance worth paying for.
Keep the cash portfolio and F&O account separate; if you must pledge, use the collateral only to hedge, never to add directional exposure.

strategies.name: Zero-cost portfolio collar
strategies.construction: Buy Nifty ETF (entry ~24,000) + buy Dec-2025 24,000 put + sell 28,000 call with equal premium
strategies.numbers: put premium ~2% of capital, financed entirely by the short call; max loss ~2% of capital even if market crashes
strategies.best_regime: euphoric markets when you want to stay invested but cap downside
strategies.adjustments: roll the put/call pair on expiry or after large moves
strategies.risks: caps upside above the sold call strike; basis risk between ETF and index

strategies.name: Pair trade (long stock / short index future)
strategies.construction: Hold a strong stock long; short index futures of equal value using pledged collateral
strategies.numbers: Bank Nifty futures carried ~400-500 point monthly rollover premium (~5-6% annualized collected on the short)
strategies.best_regime: neutral-to-bearish markets while retaining stock conviction

title_clean: Time to Invest in Mid Caps?
summary: Mid/small-cap cycle anatomy using 2016-18 (+99% in 671 days then ~50% washout) and 2022-24 (+148% in 824 days) as templates; current drop -20/21% with FIIs having sold 3+ lakh crore; warns mid/small cycles run 2 years up then ~2 years down; more price damage and a long time correction ahead; taxes and valuations are structural negatives.
lessons: Mid/small-cap trends persist: roughly two-year rallies followed by two-year flat/down phases - 'every dip is a buy' fails in the down phase.
100% up followed by 50% down equals zero return - percentage framing misleads; track levels, not percentages.
When an index rallies more than 100%, stop adding longs and start booking profits - the tail risk is asymmetric.
A one-day FII buy after months of selling means nothing; judge flows on multi-week windows.
Real return = return minus inflation minus taxes; rising STT/LTCG/GST quietly re-price every 'cheap' rally.

strategies.adjustments: scale out in tranches as the index extends beyond +100%
strategies.risks: cycles can extend; selling too early sacrifices upside

summary: Uses the frog-in-boiling-water parable to argue investors/media miss slow structural decay: India underperforming both US (+25% gap) and China (+25-30% gap in two months), losing its cost advantages (land, labor, taxes), so the 50-60% EM valuation premium must compress to ~20-25%. Expect time correction, not V-recovery; budget and RBI support failed to lift the market - a structural signal.
lessons: Step outside the system to see it: judge your market against global peers, not against its own 25-year chart.
When good news (rate cuts, OMO, swaps) fails to lift a market, something structural is wrong - don't average down on hope.
Old lows are not supports once inflation and taxes are factored in; adjust historical levels for purchasing power.
Anchors who extrapolate 'India always recovers' are the frog in heating water; past resilience was a different cost structure.
If repeated policy positives get sold every day, wait for price correction to end AND time correction to mature before re-entering.

summary: Don't stop SIPs - restructure them. Mid-cap 15-year anatomy shows ~2-year up / ~2-year flat-down cycles; after >100% index rallies, book profits and move SIP flows to debt funds for the down phase, then run a 'double SIP' on recovery. lessons: Don't stop the SIP - redirect it: in mid/small-cap down phases, route contributions to debt funds until the cycle matures (~2 years).
When a mid/small-cap index has rallied >100%, start systematic withdrawal (SWP) - the next two years historically go nowhere or down.
After a ~2-year consolidation, run a double SIP: resume equity contributions plus redeploy accumulated debt funds in tranches.
Ladder risk by regime: debt -> large-cap -> mid-cap -> small-cap, rotating contributions by 6-month blocks as the cycle turns.
Hybrid funds self-manage the equity/debt switch but must hold ~65% equity for tax reasons - a structural drag in bear phases.
